    Theorem 11.8(1): initial forms identify ray A with ray A₀ #

    main-theorems.tex (thm:final-standardness(1)): for a basic representation-finite A, in every characteristic, "initial forms identify ray A with ray A₀. In particular ray A is associative, A₀ ≅ k ray A is representation-finite".

    We state the identification as a ray presentation of A by the ray table of A₀ (rayA_eq_rayA0): the table is associative by construction, its linearization is A₀ (thetaA0), and A₀ is representation-finite (Proposition 2.10). In characteristic two the presentation is Proposition 8.3(2) (exists_normedRayBasis_char2); otherwise A ≅ A₀ (Theorem B with Corollary 4.15) and the fibre presentation of Proposition 11.3(3) with zero correction (exists_rayPres_A0).

          Theorem 11.8(3), standardness: the linearization of a finite ray category Q with kQ representation-finite is standard, in every characteristic. By Theorem 11.8(1) kQ is presented by the ray table of its A₀; by Definition 3.9 it is presented by Q; Lemma 3.6 identifies the two tables, so kQ ≅ A₀, and the converse of Corollary 4.15 applies.

                        Theorem 11.8(3), freeness of W(Q): for a finite ray category Q with kQ representation-finite, W(Q) is free abelian. Q is identified with the ray table of the algebra A₀ of kQ (Theorem 11.8(1) and Lemma 3.6), whose scalar-weight group is free.

                        theorem MultiplicativeBasisDeformations.finalStandardness_rayCategory (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {V R : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R] (Q : RaySys.Mult V R) (hQ : Q.IsFiniteRayCategory k) (hfin : IsRepresentationFinite k ↥(Q.Lin k)) :
                        Module.Free ℤ Q.W ∧ IsStandard k ↥(Q.Lin k)

                        Theorem 11.8(3) (thm:final-standardness): for every finite ray category Q with kQ representation-finite, over an algebraically closed field of any characteristic, W(Q) is free abelian and kQ is standard, k(Γ_{kQ}) ≃ ind(mod kQ).
